speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs how is the Ministry enhancing measures to mitigate against scams on the purchase and reselling of concert tickets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In this scam variant, victims would come across advertisements for concert tickets on e-commerce websites or social media platforms, such as Carousell, Facebook, Telegram and Twitter.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: When victims approach the scammers to purchase the concert tickets, scammers would often claim that the tickets are selling fast to pressure victims into making payment quickly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Once the payment is received, scammers would claim to be unable to transfer the tickets to the victim and, thereafter, become uncontactable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In some cases, victims may receive their tickets via email or WhatsApp, only to realise that the tickets are invalid on the actual day of the concert.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To combat this scam variant and scams in general, no single measure alone is adequate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Instead, we require a multi-faceted approach, including blocking scam content, enhancing the safeguards on digital platforms and public education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The SPF also worked with the platforms to prevent such scams from happening, such as through pre-emptive detection and blocking of scam accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To raise awareness of concert ticket scams, SPF partnered ticket retailers, concert organisers and online platforms to issue advisories to the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, SingPost displayed these advisories on digital screens within their outlets for members of the public who were queuing to purchase concert tickets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The TSR informs consumers on the anti-scam measures that major e-commerce marketplaces have in place, such as user verification and secure payment options.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We encourage consumers to transact only with the marketplaces with better ratings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They have not implemented the safeguards we recommended, despite repeated engagements with them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Shopee and Carousell, on the other hand, have stepped up their measures and we are glad also for the sake of their customers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Ultimately, the best defence against scams is a discerning public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We urge the public to adopt precautionary measures through the three simple steps of "Add", "Check", and "Tell".

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, "Add" the ScamShield App, anti-virus software and other security features, such as multifactor authentication for digital accounts and transaction limits for Internet banking.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: When transacting online, use secure payment options and never take transactions or payments off-platform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, "Check" the reviews of the seller and look out for potential red flags when making online purchases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Where possible, arrange for a physical meet-up with the seller to verify the authenticity of the tickets before making payment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Third, "Tell" your family and friends about scam encounters and report fraudulent advertisements to social media and e-commerce platforms, as well as to the authorities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Because of acts like Taylor Swift, Singapore is fast becoming an international hub or at least a regional hub for entertainment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is important that we safeguard the trust factor of Singapore being a place for such entertainment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: To this extent, how can the concert operators and concert promoters do more to safeguard, especially in the transfer of tickets and verification of authenticity, including to a certain extent, non-transferability of certain tickets, so that it is tagged to a particular person, making it, of course, harder to resell?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But if you want to grow this as a hub, I think it is worthwhile considering.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Indeed, today, we are seeing many popular performers, such as Taylor Swift and Coldplay.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They have chosen to perform in Singapore after the easing of the COVID-19 restrictions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We realised that the scammers took advantage of these ticket sales to these concerts to perpetrate scams.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As such, as I have shared, we continue to work and take the multifaceted approach where we work with the platform operators as well as the organisers of concerts, in this case, not only to make sure that we, as far as possible, close the gap, but at the same time, would also go upstream and share with the public on what they should look out for and always go to the authorised ticket sellers, even the resellers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will continue to work with them closely and see how we can improve the protection.
